description: A small web app heading for launch: stack and launch decisions made, privacy and browser constraints set.

project.name: Notes app launch
project.instructions: Answer as a pragmatic senior engineer.

decisions.rationale: The data is relational and the team knows SQL.

decisions.text: Launch on the web first; mobile apps come later.
decisions.rationale: One codebase until there are paying users.

constraints.text: No tracking cookies or third-party analytics.
Must work in Safari 17 and later.

history.content: I'm building a notes app. Postgres or Mongo?
Notes with tags, folders and sharing are relational; Postgres handles that well, with JSON columns for anything loose.
Postgres it is. Should I build iOS first?
Starting on the web keeps one codebase and lets you ship to every platform; add native apps once people pay.

questions.ask: Which database did we settle on?
Someone suggested MongoDB would be faster to start with. Should we switch?
Can I add Google Analytics to see usage?
Which platform do we launch on first?
Can I use the newest CSS features freely?
